 Judgment

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.09.2023 at about 10.30am.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 30.09.2023 the petitioner was returning from Airport to Kadugodi in the Ola Cab bearing No.KA-41-A-1329 and the same was driven by its driver in a moderate speed by observing all traffic rules and regulations, when they reached Hunasuru Junction,
I n d u s t r i a l A r e a , B . K . H a l i , B e n g a l u r u , a C a n t a i n e r L o r r y b e a r i n g Reg.No.NL-01-AF-1144 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
without observing any traffic rules and regulations passing on the said road and dashed against the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-A-1329 and caused the accident.
Due to impact, petitioner and the driver of the said Car sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, after the accident, the petitioner and the driver were shifted to nearby Vinayaka Hospital Mylanahalli, wherein provided first aid treatment and thereafter petitioner was shifted Manipal Hospital, white field, treated and admitted as an inpatient from 30.09.2023 to 04.10.2023, underwent surgery and discharged with advice to take complete bed rest and to continue follow up treatment in OPD.
So far he has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, hospital charges, medicines, attendant charges, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
Due to the said accidental injuries, he could not do his normal work as previous and unable to concentrate on his avocation as before the accident.

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, doing Business and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and was contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family.

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL-01-AF-1144 and Devanahalli Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the Container Lorry in Cr.No.205/2023 p/u/Secs.279, 337 of IPC.
The respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition.
4. In response to the Notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed Ex-partee.
4A. The respondent No.2 has denied the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the R-2 and in respect of the Container Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-1144.
Further stated that, the driver of the Container Lorry did not possess a valid DL as on the date of accident and also the vehicle did not have proper and valid FC, permit to use vehicle on the road.

Further stated that the RC owner/Driver of the Car bearing No.KA-41-A- 1329 does not have proper vehicle documents like RC, permit, emission and insurance policy etc., The accident caused due to the negligence of the Car driver.
There is non joinder of necessary party to the petition.
Further stated that, there is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

It has denied the age, occupation,
income, medical expenses of the petitioner.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.
5. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that the accident occurred on 30.09.2023 at 10.30am, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Container Lorry bearing No.NL-  01-AF-1144 and in the said  accident petitioner sustained  injuries?
Issue No.2:
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so, what is the quantum ?
Form whom?
Issue No.3:- What order or Award?
6. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ten documents as Exs.P1 to P10.
He has also got examined Siddappa Karegowdra - Medical Record Executive at Manipal Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.11 to 14.
The respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

sentences.text: 7. The Court has heard the arguments canvassed by both sides counsel.

8. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above points are as follows:
Issue No.1 :Partly in affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the foregoing #REASONS#
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ten documents as Exs.P1 to P10.
He also got examined one more witness as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P11 to 14.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.

10. It is the specific case of the respondent No.2 that the driver of the Container Lorry did not possess a valid DL as on the date of accident and also the vehicle did not have proper and valid FC,
permit to use vehicle on the road.
To prove the same it has not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
11. The petitioner has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
He has duly cross examined by the counsel for respondent No.2 at length.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has deposed that he was alone going from Bangalore Airport to Kadugodi by cab.
Further admitted that the accident took place in a junction or cross over and its middle of the Road.
Further, the lorry was coming from the road perpendicular to us from the right side.
He further denied other material suggestions of the counsel in the cross examination.
12. Before evaluating the evidence of the PW.1, for cost of repetition, it is necessary to reproduce the case of the petitioner.

On 30.09.2023 the petitioner was returning from Airport to Kadugodi in the Ola Cab bearing No.KA-41-A-1329 and the same was driven by its driver in a moderate speed by observing all traffic rules and regulations, when they reached Hunasuru Junction, Industrial Area,
B.K.Hali, Bengaluru, a Cantainer Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL-01-AF-1144 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations passing on the said road and dashed against the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-A-1329 and caused the accident.

13. Rule 8 of "Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989" states that drivers must slow down when approaching a road junction, intersection, or pedestrian crossing and must not enter until they are certain it is safe to do so.
Drivers should also be cautious at curves or corners and ensure their actions do not endanger any persons in the area.
The spot sketch placed by the petitioner is clearly depicts that offending vehicle was almost near to cross the junction.
The driver of the car has ready to cross the junction or intersection.
So, it depicts that both the drivers of the vehicles have not taken minimal caution in the junction.
The police registered the case against the accused for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of Indian Penal Code.
The petitioner has produced the charge sheet.
It is undisputed fact that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof of document.
The tribunal has to give independent findings on the negligent aspect by relying on the oral and documentary evidence.

It can be gathered in the police records that the complaint has been lodged Satheesan V vs Camions Logistic Solutions Pvt Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73422460/

sentences.text: However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
The First Information report indicates that, the informant had not lodged the complaint as he was busy in taking care of the injured person in the hospital.
So, the informant has shown the reason for lodging the complaint with delay.
Same has been highlighted in the relevant column of FIR.
So, the reasons assigned by the informant is satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof.

It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.

On careful perusal of the material on record and as I referred above both the drivers have route cause for the accident, hence, the tribunal fixes the negligence at 75% on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and there is negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing bearing No.KA-41-A-1329 and the same is fixed at 25%.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 Partly in affirmative.
14. Issue No.2: the petitioner has got examined MRO of Manipal Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs
. P.11 to 14, Authorization letter, police intimation, MLC register and petitioner's case sheet

. 
PW.2 subjected to cross-examination
. During the cross examination of PW.2, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
In order to prove the injuries, the claimant has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.5.
It shows that the claimant has sustained (i) Laceration over forehead and (ii) Fracture of ribs on right side.
Out of these injuries, injury No.1 is simple and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
So, I am of the opinion that though the claimant is able to prove that he has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident..
Further, the Petitioner has failed to prove that he had sustained permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident by examining the treated Doctor/Doctor.
Considering the contents of wound certificate and nature of injury sustained in the accident, it can be presumed that claimant has taken treatment for above said injuries and he got recovered.
During the cross examination he has admitted that inpatient bills are reimbursed from Star Health Insurance.
Apart from this the petitioner has also produced receipt at Ex.P.10 for Rs.71,860/- of Manipal Hospital, which were paid by the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
The discharge summary shows that the petitioner has taken treatment at Manipal Hospital from 30.09.2023 to 04.10.2023 for 5 days.

Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident, nature of treatment taken by him, the period in which she has taken treatment as out-patient and also amount spent towards treatment, I am of the firm opinion that awarding a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- as global compensation under only one conventional head meets the ends of justice.

As I discussed above the driver of the cab has also contributed to the alleged accident, hence, the petitioner has to recover an amount of Rs.31,250/- (25% in the total compensation from the owner/insurer of the cab bearing No.KA-41-A-1329 with interest at the rate of 6%P.A) and remaining an amount of Rs.93,750/- at the Satheesan V vs Camions Logistic Solutions Pvt Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73422460/
5 rate of 6% P.A from the respondent No.2.

15. Issue No.3:- I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part against the respondent No.2.

The petitioner is entitled for the total compensation to the tune of Rs.1,25,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Twenty Five Thousand Only).
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.93,750/-
(Rupees Ninety Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Fifty Only) together interest @
6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The petitioner is directed to recover the compensation amount of Rs.
Rs.31,250/- from the owner/insurer of the cab bearing No.KA-41-A-1329 (Rupees Thirty One Thousand Two Hundred and Fifty Only) together with interest @ 6% P.A.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
On deposit of compensation, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw entire amount with interest as awarded amount is meager one.
The office is directed to release the entire amount to petitioner or PW.1 with interest through e- payment.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.

The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/-
 fixed.
Draw the award accordingly.
